venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU — Faulkner’s shotgun, White’s stand-up edges
dek: Sat the 20:11 SEC condensed game. Broadcast angle. Not All-22. This is what Buster Faulkner called and what Brad White lined up — from the cut, not the box.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — 20:11 SEC condensed game sat (Charles Drive upload). Broadcast condensed, not All-22, not every snap. Charles has not approved publish. Fan rail stays empty.

sources.label: Official box (stats only — support after the snap)

headline: Faulkner lives in no-huddle shotgun and lets Baugh and the quick game cook. White plays 4-down with stand-up edges and mixes the shell. The leaks are contain and the fade.

offense.kicker: Buster Faulkner — what he is designing
offense.body:
Faulkner’s base on this tape is no-huddle shotgun, 11 personnel: one back, one tight end, three out. He does not huddle. He gets lined up and plays. That is the install fans can see without All-22.

The run is built around Jadan Baugh (No. 13). Inside zone is the early-down answer — Baugh hits it, or he bounces when the front clogs. Faulkner is not only shotgun: on the second scoring drive he puts Baugh under center and tosses it, and Baugh breaks a tackle in the backfield and wins the edge. Later the red zone is downhill — pad down, puller, finish. Three rushing touchdowns, three different answers: backside cut, bounce-and-pad, power through the pile.

The pass game is rhythm, then a shot. Opening score: Aaron Philo (No. 12) gets it out now to Vernell Brown III (No. 1). First man misses. Brown races it 49 yards. That is Faulkner’s quick game — not a jump-ball. Next trip: Philo to Bailey Stockton (No. 3) and Stockton finishes at the pylon. After FAU punches in, Faulkner max-protects and Philo throws the deep ball to TJ Abrams (No. 4) down the right side — the 63-yarder that puts them at the door. Then empty at the 3: the edges climb, Philo keeps, he walks it in.

He uses motion. Jet and play-action show up after Baugh has already won. Duke Clark (No. 20) is the second-back finisher — drag for a touchdown, gap run standing up, and the late carries when Baugh is done. Tramell Jones Jr. (No. 9) takes the last drive. The cut does not give us a full Jones grade. It shows Faulkner did not close the laptop.

What condensed still hides: every first-and-second down RPO, the protection slide, who won which gap on the 61-yarder. We saw Baugh rip the long one that set up the 6-yard score. We are not inventing Wildcat from a wide camera.
bullets: Base: no-huddle shotgun, 11 personnel. Tempo is the identity.
Baugh: inside zone, toss, bounce, power. Three TDs, three looks.
Quick game: Brown III 49 after the first man misses. Stockton to the pylon.
The shot: max protect, Philo to Abrams down the right sideline.
Red zone: empty keep by Philo; Clark as the closer.
Motion and play-action after the run is real. That is Faulkner, not freestyle.

defense.kicker: Brad White — what he is lining up
defense.body:
White’s look on this condensed cut is a 4-down surface with stand-up edges — two hands in the dirt, two ends who can rush or drop. That is the Saturday tell. He is not stuck there. On 3rd-and-10 empty to open the night he shows 3-down, linebackers walking, then a 4-man rush into a zone drop. FAU’s first drive lives on hitch, flat, and out. Then the ball comes out late and DJ Coleman (No. 33) ends it at the Florida 6.

He mixes one-high and two-high. Off coverage on the outside is how Veltkamp (No. 10) moves the chains early — complete, rally, tackle. Myles Graham (No. 5) and the back seven show up in the pile. That is not a hold. That is a first-quarter drive that keeps converting until the takeaway.

The leaks on this tape are the ones fans already felt. Goal line: White packs the box and still loses the phone booth to Ethan Ervin. Third-and-goal: 3-down, stand-up edges, Veltkamp flushes and dives the pylon — Kamran James (No. 24) is in the picture; contain lost. Late: Kelby Valsin (No. 2) beats J’Vari Flowers (No. 6) and FAU punches the 20-yard score. Same family as Stockton the other way — fade / boundary, lost leverage.

The other takeaway on the scoring package still stands: A-gap heat, Veltkamp off the back foot, Dijon Johnson (No. 27) high-points it, Coleman on the breakup. Condensed also shows White getting off the field on fourth down in the second half. Do not turn 21 points into a season identity, and do not write a “lockdown” essay from a cut that skips the long FAU drives.

Bett’s strip is on the official chart in the fourth. This camera does not give a clean All-22 of the rush plan. We are not inventing the stunt.
bullets: Base look: 4-down, stand-up edges. Mixes 3-down on obvious pass.
Shell: one-high and two-high. Do not name Cover 3 from this camera.
Coleman: 3rd-and-10, empty, drive dies at the Florida 6.
Johnson: back-foot duck after interior heat. High-point.
Leaks: Ervin phone-booth dive; Veltkamp pylon scramble; Valsin vs Flowers.
Graham, James, Bett show up. This is not a full-snap grade.

specials.kicker: Specials — the kick on the cut
specials.body: Patrick Durkin from 53, 4th-and-4, 2:12 of the first. Left hash, clean operation, down the middle. Makes it 17–0. Kickoffs on this cut are touchbacks. Florida never punts on the package. Unused punter stays a box fact.
bullets: No Florida punt on this tape.

keys: Faulkner: no-huddle shotgun 11. Zone and toss for Baugh, then quick game and one deep shot.
Philo: ball out on time; empty keep when the edges climb; the Abrams ball is the shot.
White: 4-down, stand-up edges, mix the high safety. Default rush is four.
Who stood out on this cut: Baugh, Philo, Brown III, Stockton, Abrams, Clark, Coleman, Durkin.
The leaks: contain (Veltkamp) and the fade (Valsin / Flowers). Campbell will test both.
Not All-22. Do not invent coverage names or a Wildcat we did not clearly see.

nextWeek.look: Home Saturday 5:30. Faulkner will live in shotgun tempo again. White has to set the edge and win the fade. That is what this cut actually showed.
